statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 13% sits in the low band, below the 20% watch threshold and well below the 25% block level.
recommendation: Tail remains below both the watch and the block threshold. The 6 October cash session set a 31,361.37 record intraday high, then granted and extended a full retracement to close at a record 31,224.47, only 16 points above the session low. VIX eased to 15.01 near its session low and the 10-year slipped to 5.27%, so mean reversion is functioning and no amplifier set is aligned. Stress stays elevated at 45% on long-end yields near multi-decade highs and WTI close to $90. The published danger window spans the 10-year note auction and the FOMC minutes on 7 October, 17:00Z to 19:00Z.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at a record 31,224.47 after granting a full retracement from its 31,361.37 high; NQ firms to 31,501 into the globex halt and Tail eases to 13% with the FOMC minutes next
body: The 6 October US cash session closed with the Nasdaq-100 at 31,224.47, up 148.03 points or 0.48%, a record close set after a 31,361.37 record intraday high earlier in the day. The decisive observation for this hour is the shape of that close: price finished 0.44% below the record high and only 16.27 points above the 31,208.20 session low, so the retracement off the high was granted and then extended into the bell. That is the signature of functioning mean reversion, not of a pathological no-retracement path, and it is why Tail eases to 13% even with the index at an all-time high. The session low still held 0.42% above Monday's 31,076.44 record close, leaving the gap above the prior record unfilled and the daily uptrend structurally intact, which is why the dominant mode is read as mixed rather than trend-up. Breadth of the advance was wide across the majors, with the S&P 500 at a record 7,818.93 (+0.58%), the Nasdaq Composite at a back-to-back record 27,599.79 (+0.45%) and the Dow at 51,521.28 (+0.49%). Semiconductors participated but faded similarly, with SOX closing 13,217.82 (+0.34%) near its own session low and 0.99% under its high. Nvidia touched all-time highs with its market capitalisation approaching $6 trillion, AMD set fresh records, and Marvell rose roughly 8% on raised 2028 revenue guidance. After the cash close, NQ December futures firmed to 31,501.00 (+0.59%) into the 21:00Z globex halt, which leaves them 0.37% under the 31,616.50 futures session high and in the upper half of the day's range. That post-close firming is a mild offset to the weak cash close, but it is a thin tape and it does not constitute persistent directional efficiency. Cross-asset confirmation is mostly risk-supportive this hour: VIX closed 15.01, down 3.29%, at the low end of a 14.96-15.54 range, and the 10-year eased to 5.27% from a 5.31% close that marked a 24-year high. The genuine stress inputs are structural rather than acute. Long-end yields remain near multi-decade highs with the 30-year at 5.64%, approaching 2002 levels, and the 2-year at 4.84% on the latest published H.15 leaves the curve steep. WTI at $89.91 closed near the top of a wide $86.86-$90.05 range, and reporting continues to flag diesel costs, so the energy-to-yields channel stays live. Those factors hold Stress at 45% in the elevated band while leaving Tail in the low band, which is the expected configuration when a difficult environment still grants retracements. No verified new geopolitical escalation with market transmission was identified for this hour; a background Middle East risk premium is consistent with oil near $90 but is not evidence of discontinuity, and equities closing at records with VIX down 3.3% argues against acute transmission. Confidence is set at 86%. Verified current levels are held across the index, futures, volatility, rates, oil and semiconductors, alongside an independently confirmed Wednesday calendar. It is reduced slightly from the prior hour because futures are in the 21:00Z-22:00Z halt so there is no live price path at the assessment instant, the shared Finviz context file is roughly seven days stale and unusable, and the 2-year yield is from the 5 October H.15 release. The forward path is shaped almost entirely by the Wednesday US calendar. Tail is expected to ease through the Asian hours to a 9% trough between 04:00Z and 05:00Z, with a small bump at 23:00Z for the Fed Logan speech because a hawkish tone in thin liquidity is a plausible air pocket. It then rebuilds with the European open and the US pre-market before stepping to 18% for the 13:00Z cash-open hour, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks from a record close is the specific pattern that would deny mean reversion. The watch band is entered at 15:00Z and the forecast peaks at 23% in the 18:00Z FOMC minutes hour. That peak stays below the 25% block threshold because it rests on a scheduled multi-stage event rather than on observed one-way structure, consistent with treating event importance as primarily a Stress and Confidence input until the price path confirms otherwise. The danger window is kept narrow at 17:00Z to 19:00Z on 7 October, spanning the 10-year note auction, the minutes themselves and the hour in which a delayed second leg would surface.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment, so the window is complete. Tail opened the window at 14% at 21:00Z on 5 October, drifted down through the Asian hours to an 8% low at 05:00Z as the index mean-reverted in thin liquidity, then rebuilt steadily with the European and US sessions to a 22% peak at 15:00Z on 6 October around the record-high push. It fell back to 17-20% through the afternoon as the retracement off the high was granted, and closed the window at 14% for the 20:00Z cash-close hour. Stress ran a narrow 45-49% band throughout, never leaving the elevated reading that long-end yields and oil have sustained. Confidence held between 86% and 88%. Dominant mode ran mixed through the overnight hours, switched to trend-up from 10:00Z as the European and US sessions built the record-high advance, and returned to mixed for the final hour once the close near the session low confirmed that mean reversion was still working.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to ease through the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins, reaching a 9% trough between 04:00Z and 05:00Z, with a modest 13% bump at 23:00Z for the Fed Logan speech because a hawkish tone in thin liquidity is a plausible air pocket. It rebuilds with the European open and the US pre-market, then steps up into the 7 October US session: 18% for the 13:00Z cash-open hour, 19% through the EIA crude release, 20% as Consumer Inflation Expectations print at 15:00Z and the watch band is entered, 22% for the 17:00Z 10-year note auction and a 23% peak in the 18:00Z FOMC minutes hour. That peak stays inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold because it rests on a scheduled multi-stage event rather than on observed one-way structure. Tail then falls back to 21% for the post-minutes repricing hour and 18% by the Wednesday cash close, on the assumption that price discovery is orderly and retracements are granted. Stress tracks the same shape from 45% now to a 41% overnight trough and a 52% peak at the minutes. The published danger window is held narrow at 17:00Z to 19:00Z on 7 October. The main invalidations are an overnight drive beyond the 31,616.50 NQ futures high without a pullback, an abnormally wide pre-market gap, a weak 10-year auction transmitting into equities, or a Wednesday close near the session high after a hawkish minutes reaction.
